C05-M04-L01-F1.title: Inside a network vulnerability scanner
C05-M04-L01-F1.caption: The scanner pipeline from an authorised target list to results with confidence, with the feed as a separate input to check selection.
C05-M04-L01-F1.alt: Pipeline graph: Target list + authorisation leads to Discovery (which hosts are alive), then Port and service detection (product names and versions into the knowledge base), then Check selection (driven by what service detection recorded), then Test execution (version comparisons, active probes, configuration checks), then Results with confidence (severity, evidence, detection confidence). A separate Feed box (checks as data, updated daily) points into Check selection.

C05-M04-L01-F2.title: Scanner detection methods ranked by evidence strength
C05-M04-L01-F2.caption: Detection methods from the weakest evidence (a banner) to the strongest (a safe proof), with false-positive risk moving the other way.
C05-M04-L01-F2.alt: Table with columns Method, What is observed, Evidence strength and False-positive risk. Banner or header version: a label the target chose to send; weak; high. Remote behaviour probe: response to a crafted request; medium; medium. Configuration observation: a visible setting such as a missing header; medium-strong; low. Authenticated package check: installed package versions; strong; low. Safe proof of exploit: behaviour the target cannot fake; strongest; very low. Rows are coloured from red for the weakest evidence to green for the strongest.
rows: A label the target chose to send
A visible setting, e.g. missing header
C05-M04-L01-F2.note: The weaker the method, the more validation a result needs before it is reported.
